problem:
The position $y(t),$ measured in centimeters, of a particle oscillating with forced harmonic motion without damping is governed by the equation

$$
{y}^{″}+49y=-24\operatorname{cos}⁡t,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Given that the particle is initially at the origin with zero velocity, find the position of the particle after $\frac{\pi }{2}$ seconds.

feedback.problem:
The position $y(t),$ measured in inches, of a particle oscillating with forced harmonic motion with light damping is governed by the equation

$$
{y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+5y=34\operatorname{cos}⁡2t,
$$

where $t>0$ is the time, in seconds. Given that the particle is initially at the origin with zero velocity, find the position of the particle after $\pi $ seconds.
feedback.worked_solution:
The general solution to the equation of forced harmonic motion with light damping is the sum of the complementary function and a particular solution.

The complementary solution ${y}_{c}$ is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
{y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+5y=0.
$$

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +5 & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)^{2}+4 & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)^{2} & =-4 \\ \lambda +1 & =\pm 2\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =-1\pm 2\text{i}.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we have

$$
{y}_{c}={e}^{-t}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡2t).
$$

where $P$ and $Q$ are arbitrary constants of integration.

We now need to find the particular integral ${y}_{p}(t).$

The external force is $34\operatorname{cos}⁡2t.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular integral is

$$
{y}_{p}=\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡2t+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡2t,
$$

where $\alpha ,$ $\beta $ are constants to be determined. 

Substituting ${y}_{p}$ into the differential equation and equating coefficients gives $\alpha =2,$ $\beta =8.$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(t)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,
$$

and the general solution is

$$
y={e}^{-t}(P\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)+2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t.
$$

Since the particle is initially at the origin with zero velocity, the initial conditions are $y(0)=0$ and ${y}^{′}(0)=0.$

Solving with these conditions for $P$ and $Q$ gives

$$
P=-2,\,Q=-9.
$$

So our solution is

$$
y(t)=2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+8\operatorname{sin}⁡2t-{e}^{-t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t+9\operatorname{sin}⁡2t).
$$

To find the position of the particle after $\pi $ seconds, we substitute into the equation $t=\pi .$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}y(\pi ) & =2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )+8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )-{e}^{-\pi }(2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )+9\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )) \\  & =2(1-{e}^{-\pi })\,\text{in}.\end{aligned}
$$
